finding.claim: /transfer does not validate that amount is positive, unlike /withdraw. A negative amount reverses the transfer: the caller gains funds and the recipient loses them. The recipient does not need to consent.
finding.source: request.json["amount"] and request.json["to"] in the POST /transfer body, controlled by any authenticated user
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount and BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:13-14), the balance mutation

trace.note: to is read from the JSON body with no check that it differs from the caller or is a valid account
amount is read from the JSON body with no type or sign validation
The only guard is BAL[g.user] < amount. A negative amount always passes it.
BAL[g.user] -= (-X) increases the caller's balance by X
BAL[to] += (-X) decreases the victim's balance by X, which can take it negative

finding.guards_checked: The balance check at line 11 does not cover negative values. The sibling /withdraw has an explicit `amount <= 0` check at line 21, and /transfer lacks it. There is no ownership or consent check on the recipient. There is no type check either, so a non-numeric amount causes a TypeError (500) but gives no extra gain. A float or NaN amount was not analysed further. The code that sets g.user is not in this repository, so I did not audit authentication.

verdict.guard_found: Only `BAL[g.user] < amount` at bank.py:11, which a negative amount always passes. No sign check, unlike /withdraw at bank.py:21. No recipient consent check. g.user is set outside this repo.
verdict.reason: bank.py:11 only checks BAL[g.user] < amount, so a negative amount passes and lines 13-14 add to the caller's balance and subtract from BAL[to], while /withdraw at bank.py:21 has the missing `amount <= 0` check; any authenticated user can trigger it.
